source: Hacknet roguelite plan, section 16 (milestone roadmap), sections 7 to 12A

milestones.title: M2: Roguelite shell
milestones.description: Procedural seeded network generation, a contract board, the hub/shop between runs, persistent credits and unlocks, the full breach layer stack (proxy overload, firewall rule-reading, privesc), and the trace to SOC reaction thresholds. Independently playable.

issues.title: feat: network generator v2 with subnets and node types
issues.body:
Grow the seeded generator from one small company into layered subnets (edge/DMZ, internal, crown jewels) with harder defenses and bigger payouts the deeper you go.

**Scope**
- Node types: contract targets, loot caches (tools, wordlists, creds), safe relays (pivot points that lower heat), honeypots (raise heat fast).
- Network size, defense layers and heat sensitivity scale with difficulty.
- Same seed gives the same network so runs can be replayed and shared.

**Done when**
- [ ] Generator produces at least 3 subnet depths with all 4 node types
- [ ] Honeypots are recognizable to a careful player (Index entry explains the tells)
- [ ] Unit tests cover determinism per seed and reachability of every contract target

Plan: sections 8 and 16 (M2).

issues.title: feat: contract board with 3 to 6 jobs per op
issues.body:
Replace the fixed three contracts with a board generated per op from contract templates.

**Scope**
- Templates for Recon, Breach-and-retrieve, Breach-and-destroy, Log analysis and Web (section 9), filled from the generated network.
- Each job shows payout, faction, difficulty and the skill it teaches.
- Completing a job can reveal deeper nodes.
- Verification by real output: flag string, file hash, deleted/created file, or a submitted answer.

**Done when**
- [ ] Board shows 3 to 6 jobs drawn from at least 5 templates
- [ ] Every template has a test proving it is solvable on generated networks

Plan: sections 8 and 9.

issues.title: feat: hub between runs (rig, shop, board and Heat select)
issues.body:
Add the between-runs hub: the player's apartment/rig.

**Scope**
- Shop, story chat, pick a contract board (faction) and a difficulty (Heat).
- Run summary on return: payout, heat, Index entries unlocked.
- Extract options: full board, early extract (partial), traced (reduced payout, keep banked loot and permanent unlocks).

**Done when**
- [ ] A full run loop works: hub, op, extract or traced, back to hub
- [ ] Hub works with keyboard only

Plan: section 8.

issues.title: feat: persistent meta-progression and versioned saves
issues.body:
Persist what carries across runs and make saves safe to evolve.

**Persists:** credits, per-faction rep and unlocked tiers, owned tools and mods, RAM and rig upgrades, wordlists and the banked cred DB, `~/bin` scripts (later), unlocked man pages and skill certs, story progress.
**Resets per run:** network, board, in-run heat, temporary creds (unless banked).

**Done when**
- [ ] Save format has a version number and a migration path from the M1 save
- [ ] Tests cover save, load and migration
- [ ] Desktop build stores saves in the app data dir (not only localStorage)

Plan: section 8.

issues.title: feat: proxy layer and floodctl overload
issues.body:
Add the proxy defense layer, beaten by overloading it with `floodctl` run from owned relays.

**Scope**
- More owned relays overload faster; flooding is loud and raises the trace.
- Proxy-pierce tool mod lets specific tools work through an active proxy.
- Index entry: load/DoS concept, pivoting, detection and defense.

**Done when**
- [ ] Proxied hosts block crackers until the proxy is overloaded
- [ ] Tests cover overload math and heat cost

Plan: sections 7.2 and 11.

issues.title: feat: privilege escalation layer (sudo -l, SUID, cron)
issues.body:
Split foothold from root: a user shell is easy, root needs reading the box and finding one real misconfiguration.

**Scope**
- Commands: `sudo -l`, `find / -perm -4000`, cron and kernel checks on owned boxes.
- Generated misconfigs: sudo NOPASSWD on a GTFOBins-style binary, writable cron script, SUID binary.
- Index entries for each misconfig with detection and hardening.

**Done when**
- [ ] Hosts can grant user-level access without root
- [ ] At least 3 privesc paths, each with tests

Plan: section 7.2.

issues.title: feat: SOC reaction thresholds on the trace meter
issues.body:
Make the SOC react as heat climbs.

**Scope**
- 50%: an analyst starts correlating logs (visible as mail/chatter, faster heat from repeat noise).
- 75%: your source IP is blocked; you must pivot through a new relay.
- 100%: traced, run ends.
- Optional `tracekill` panic button: rare and expensive.

**Done when**
- [ ] Each threshold has a clear on-screen event and an Index link
- [ ] Tests cover the block-and-pivot path

Plan: section 7.3.

issues.title: feat: new port crackers (SMTP, SQL, SSL chaining)
issues.body:
Add the remaining breach tools from the tool map.

**Scope**
- `smtpprobe` (25): open relay, VRFY user enumeration; enumerated users feed the SSH wordlist.
- `sqlprobe` / `sqli` (1433): default DB creds, SQL injection, dumped creds reused across the network.
- `sslchain` (443): needs another port open first (SSLTrojan-style).
- Each tool implements `ToolDef`, has a `man` page and an Index entry.

**Done when**
- [ ] Tools are buyable in the shop and appear in generated networks
- [ ] Tests per tool

Plan: sections 7.2 and 11.

issues.title: feat: tool mods v2 (Turbo, Lean, Proxy-pierce, Auto-chain)
issues.body:
Per-tool mods that change behavior, not just numbers.

- Turbo: faster but louder.
- Lean: lower RAM cost.
- Proxy-pierce: works through an active proxy.
- Auto-chain: auto-routes through an open port.

**Done when**
- [ ] Mods are shop items, stack rules are defined and tested

Plan: section 11.

milestones.title: M3: Bash scripting + Workshop v1
milestones.description: A ~/bin that persists, a nano-style in-game editor, saving and running .sh scripts that cost RAM, and the first scripting contracts. Workshop v1: Bash tools registered through the common ToolDef interface, the Range test network, and the first two homemade tools (port scanner and log watcher).

issues.title: feat: persistent ~/bin and PATH lookup for player scripts
issues.body:
Player scripts saved to `~/bin` persist across runs and are callable by name (`crack_all`) in any op.

**Done when**
- [ ] `~/bin` survives runs and save/load
- [ ] Command dispatch checks built-ins, then `~/bin`
- [ ] Running a script shows it in `ps` with a RAM cost

Plan: sections 12 and 16 (M3).

issues.title: feat: in-game nano-style editor
issues.body:
A full-screen terminal editor for scripts and Workshop tools.

**Scope**
- Open, edit, save (`^O`), exit (`^X`), search, line numbers, Bash and Python syntax highlight.
- Works inside xterm.js; no external editor needed.
- Optional later: external file hook for the desktop build.

**Done when**
- [ ] `nano ~/bin/crack_all.sh` edits and saves a file in the VFS
- [ ] Keyboard shortcuts listed in a footer like real nano

Plan: section 16 (M3).

issues.title: feat: Bash interpreter subset for .sh scripts
issues.body:
Run player `.sh` files against the simulated command set.

**Scope**
- Variables, `if`, `for`/`while`, functions, exit codes, `$()`, `$@` args, `&&` / `||`, redirection.
- Scripts cost RAM while running and can be killed with `kill`.
- Hard limits on loop iterations and runtime so a bad loop cannot freeze the game.

**Done when**
- [ ] The `crack_all.sh` example from the plan runs end to end
- [ ] Unit tests for each language feature and the runaway-loop guard

Plan: section 12.

issues.title: content: first scripting contracts (ten identical boxes)
issues.body:
Contracts that make scripting feel necessary, each introducing exactly one concept: a loop, then conditionals, then functions, then parsing output, then error handling.

**Done when**
- [ ] At least 3 scripting contracts with a timer that is miserable by hand and easy with a loop
- [ ] Verification checks the outcome (all boxes owned), not code style
- [ ] Index entries for Bash loops and exit codes

Plan: sections 9, 10 (tier 3) and 12.

issues.title: feat(workshop): Workshop v1 framework for Bash tools
issues.body:
Let the player write tools, not just scripts, and use them like shop tools.

**Scope**
- `workshop new <name> --lang bash` scaffolds from a template with one TODO.
- `workshop test <name>` runs it in the Range.
- `workshop register <name>` registers it through the existing `ToolDef` registry with `origin: workshop`, so it uses the same RAM bar, progress bar and `ps`.
- Shop UI lists them under "Your tools"; tool mods can apply.

**Done when**
- [ ] A registered Bash tool is usable in a run exactly like a bought tool
- [ ] Tests cover register, persist and run

Plan: section 12A.

issues.title: feat(workshop): the Range test network
issues.body:
A safe practice network with known answers: no heat, no payout.

**Scope**
- Fixed hosts with known open/filtered ports, banners and logs.
- Pass/fail checklist per tool type, e.g. "found all 4 open ports", "did not crash on a filtered port".

**Done when**
- [ ] Checklists exist for scanner and log watcher tools
- [ ] Range never affects run state or the trace

Plan: section 12A.

issues.title: feat(workshop): homemade port scanner (myscan)
issues.body:
First offensive Workshop tool.

**Scope**
- Template and sim API calls for TCP connect checks with timeouts and banners.
- Unlocks after owning the shop scanner and finishing the first recon contract.
- Index: TCP connect vs SYN scanning, timeouts, service banners; "Built by you" badge.

**Done when**
- [ ] A correct `myscan` passes the Range checklist and works in runs

Plan: section 12A.

issues.title: feat(workshop): homemade log watcher (watchlog)
issues.body:
First defensive Workshop tool.

**Scope**
- Tail `auth.log`, count failures per IP, alert over a threshold.
- Unlocks after the first log-analysis contract.
- Index: log monitoring, thresholds, false positives.

**Done when**
- [ ] A correct `watchlog` passes the Range checklist
- [ ] Usable in blue-team contracts

Plan: section 12A.

milestones.title: M4: Python scripting + curriculum tiers
milestones.description: Pyodide sandbox, the Python breach API, curriculum tiers 4 to 7, skill certs in the hub. Workshop v2: Python tools (SSH cracker, web dir buster), IDS rules and the auto-responder, stats derived from the player's code, Built by you Index badges, and the your rig gets attacked defense event.

issues.title: feat: Pyodide sandbox for player Python
issues.body:
Run player Python safely inside the game.

**Scope**
- Pyodide in a Web Worker, lazy-loaded so startup stays fast.
- Interrupt and timeouts (KeyboardInterrupt via SharedArrayBuffer; configure COOP/COEP for dev server and Tauri).
- No real network or filesystem: only the injected sim API is visible.
- Memory and runtime caps that map to in-game RAM.

**Done when**
- [ ] An infinite loop can be killed from `kill` without reloading
- [ ] Tests or a checklist prove `import socket`, `js`, `pyodide.http` and file access cannot reach the host
- [ ] Works in browser and desktop builds

Plan: sections 12, 14 and 15.

issues.title: feat: Python breach API
issues.body:
The `breach` module player code imports.

**Scope**
- `breach.subnet()`, `scan()`, `crack()`, `loot()`, `tcp_connect()`, `banner()`, `report()`.
- Later expansions: concurrency, event hooks (react to a trace), netmap graph object, logging/report API for blue-team automation.
- In-game docs styled like real Python docs.

**Done when**
- [ ] The `auto_breach.py` and `myscan.py` examples from the plan run
- [ ] API reference available via `man breach`

Plan: sections 11 and 12.

issues.title: feat(workshop): Workshop v2 Python tools (mybrute, mybust)
issues.body:
Python Workshop tools.

- `mybrute` SSH cracker: dictionary loops, rate limiting, lockout handling. Unlocks after the first `sshbrute` success.
- `mybust` web dir buster: HTTP status codes, wordlists, response-size heuristics. Unlocks after the first `webscan`.
- `workshop new <name> --lang python` templates and Range checklists for both.

**Done when**
- [ ] Both tools register and run in ops like shop tools

Plan: section 12A.

issues.title: feat(workshop): IDS rules and auto-responder (ban_ip)
issues.body:
Defensive Workshop tools.

- IDS rules (`rules/*.rule`): signature vs threshold detection, false positives, Snort/Sigma-style. Unlocks the first time heat crosses 50%.
- `ban_ip` auto-responder: fail2ban-style blocking and why automated response can lock out real users. Unlocks after owning `watchlog`.

**Done when**
- [ ] Rules and responder run in blue-team contracts and the rig-attack event

Plan: section 12A.

issues.title: feat(workshop): derive tool stats from the player's code
issues.body:
Good code makes a better tool.

- RAM cost from script size plus peak memory.
- Runtime from simulated packet count.
- Heat from how noisy it is (a 65k-port sweep is loud; a targeted list is quiet).
- Script efficiency perks from the shop apply.

**Done when**
- [ ] Stats are shown on register and in `tools`
- [ ] Tests show a targeted scanner beats a full sweep on heat

Plan: sections 11 and 12A.

issues.title: feat: Built by you Index badges and Mastered state
issues.body:
Registering a homemade tool adds a "Built by you" badge to the concept's Index entry and unlocks its deeper sub-section (the Mastered state).

**Done when**
- [ ] Badge and Mastered sub-section render for each Workshop tool concept

Plan: sections 12A and 13.

issues.title: feat: your rig gets attacked defense event
issues.body:
A rival brute-forces your relay. A `watchlog` plus IDS rule that catches them before their trace completes wins the event; the defensive mirror of the breach.

**Done when**
- [ ] Event triggers after the player owns at least one defensive tool
- [ ] Clear win/lose outcomes with Index links

Plan: section 12A.

issues.title: content: curriculum tiers 4 to 7 and skill certs in the hub
issues.body:
Contracts and Index entries for tiers 4 (networking), 5 (credential and service attacks), 6 (web vulns) and 7 (scripting up in Python), plus skill certs shown in the hub.

**Done when**
- [ ] Each tier has contracts, Index entries and a cert earned when its entries are unlocked and read

Plan: section 10.

milestones.title: M5: Blue team + content depth
milestones.description: Forensics and log-analysis tooling, SOC catch the attacker contracts, crypto contracts, more factions and story chat, Heat/Ascension difficulty.

issues.title: feat: forensics tooling (strings, carving, pcapview, memforensics)
issues.body:
Tools for forensics contracts: `strings`, file carving and metadata, `pcapview`, `memforensics`, timeline building, and `awk`/`cut`/`sort | uniq -c` coverage for log work.

**Done when**
- [ ] Each tool has a man page, an Index entry and tests

Plan: sections 9 and 10 (tier 9).

issues.title: content: SOC catch the attacker contracts
issues.body:
Blue-team contracts where the player investigates an intrusion (sometimes their own earlier run): find the attacker IP and compromised account, build a timeline, map IOCs to MITRE ATT&CK.

**Done when**
- [ ] At least 4 SOC contracts using logs, pcap and memory artifacts

Plan: sections 9 and 10.

issues.title: content: crypto contracts
issues.body:
Encoding vs encryption, Caesar/XOR/base64, hashing and hashcat-style cracking. Verification by submitted plaintext.

**Done when**
- [ ] At least 4 crypto contracts with Index entries

Plan: sections 9 and 10 (tier 8).

issues.title: content: more factions and story chat
issues.body:
New factions with their own contract boards, rep tiers and story chat in the hub, in the stylized cyberpunk tone.

**Done when**
- [ ] At least 2 new factions with rep-gated boards and story arcs

Plan: sections 8 and 17.1.

issues.title: feat: Heat / Ascension difficulty levels
issues.body:
Stackable difficulty for replay: higher Heat means bigger networks, more defense layers, tighter RAM, more sensitive SOC, less hand-holding, and better payouts.

**Done when**
- [ ] Heat levels selectable in the hub with clear modifiers
- [ ] Tests for modifier application

Plan: sections 8 and 9.

milestones.title: M6: Polish + companion
milestones.description: Audio/synthwave, themes, juice; data-driven contract authoring and validator (modding); then scope the phone companion (OSINT minigames, notifications, script editor) on the shared TS core.

issues.title: feat: synthwave soundtrack, SFX pass and mixer
issues.body:
Music and sound that match the neon tone: breach, crack, trace-alarm and UI SFX, a music track set, and a mixer with mute and per-channel volume.

**Done when**
- [ ] Settings persist; audio never autoplays before user interaction

Plan: section 16 (M6).

issues.title: feat: terminal themes and cosmetics shop
issues.body:
Terminal themes, prompt styles and synthwave tracks as a cosmetic credit sink (Hacknet ThemeChanger style).

**Done when**
- [ ] At least 4 themes, all meeting contrast for readability

Plan: section 11.

issues.title: feat: game feel pass (breach animations, glitch, screen effects)
issues.body:
Juice: satisfying breach animations, glitch and CRT effects, trace-alarm escalation, root celebration. Respect a reduced-motion setting.

**Done when**
- [ ] Effects can be toggled and honor prefers-reduced-motion

Plan: sections 16 (M6) and 17.1.

issues.title: feat: data-driven contract authoring and validator (modding)
issues.body:
Move contracts to a data format (JSON/YAML) with a schema and a validator CLI, so new contracts (and mods) can be authored without touching engine code.

**Done when**
- [ ] Existing contracts migrated to the data format
- [ ] `npm run validate:content` runs in CI and fails on bad content
- [ ] Authoring guide in CONTRIBUTING

Plan: section 16 (M6).

issues.title: build: sign installers and enable the Tauri auto-updater
issues.body:
Make releases trustworthy to install.

**Scope**
- Windows code signing and macOS signing plus notarization in the release workflow (secrets in GitHub environments).
- Tauri updater with a signing key and `latest.json` uploaded by tauri-action.
- Build provenance attestations for release assets.

**Done when**
- [ ] Installers open without SmartScreen/Gatekeeper warnings
- [ ] An installed build updates itself to the next release

issues.title: docs: scope the phone companion app
issues.body:
Write a scoping doc for the companion on the shared TypeScript core: OSINT minigames, notifications, script editor, and how progress syncs with the PC save. PC stays first; this is a scope, not a build.

**Done when**
- [ ] Doc covers features, tech options (Tauri mobile vs PWA), sync model and a recommended first slice

Plan: sections 16 (M6) and 17.1.

unscheduled.title: chore: format src and tests with Prettier in one commit
unscheduled.body:
Prettier currently skips `neontrace/src/`, `tests/`, `index.html` and `README.md` because that code predates the formatter (see `neontrace/.prettierignore`).

Once in-flight game PRs have merged:
1. Remove those lines from `.prettierignore`.
2. Run `npm run format` as a single `style:` commit with no other changes.
3. Add that commit SHA to a root `.git-blame-ignore-revs` so `git blame` skips it.

**Done when**
- [ ] `npm run format:check` covers all source

unscheduled.title: chore: re-enable consistent-type-imports lint rule
unscheduled.body: `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` was left off when ESLint was introduced because enabling it needs source edits (8 imports that are type-only). Turn it on and run `npm run lint:fix` in a quiet moment between feature PRs.

unscheduled.title: chore: drop the TypeScript 6 lint shim once typescript-eslint supports TS 7
unscheduled.body: The game compiles with TypeScript 7 (installed as `@typescript/native`), while `typescript` is held at 6.0.x only because typescript-eslint needs the JS compiler API. When a stable typescript-eslint release supports TS 7, move `typescript` back to 7.x, remove the alias, point `npm run typecheck` back at `tsc`, and remove the Dependabot ignore rule.

unscheduled.title: test: raise engine coverage and ratchet the floor
unscheduled.body: Coverage is about 44% of lines with a floor of 35% in `neontrace/vite.config.ts`. Add tests for `game.ts` command paths and content definitions, then raise the thresholds to just below the new numbers so coverage can only go up.
